v.why: With batch 4-10 the effective penalty alpha/batch is largest, so raising alpha over-shrinks weights and hurts more.
At tiny lr nets are undertrained after 243 epochs and wider nets change their function faster per step, substituting for lr.
Under Adam the effective functional step grows with fan-in, so wide nets hit instability at lower lr.
Narrow 16-40-unit nets are capacity-bottlenecked, so extra layers supply capacity that wide nets already have.
With tiny lr the update count is the limiting resource, and larger batches cut it at a fixed epoch budget, worsening underfit.
With batch 4-10 Adam takes many noisy steps per epoch, so raising lr reaches instability sooner than with larger batches.
3-layer ReLU nets amplify parameter perturbations multiplicatively across layers, so higher lr destabilizes them more.
Only at mid lr can deeper nets be optimized well enough to show a capacity benefit; at low lr they undertrain and at high lr they diverge.
Weight shrinkage compounds multiplicatively across three layers and collapses the signal toward a constant predictor.
Wider ReLU nets can represent the same function with smaller per-weight norms, partially escaping a heavy L2 penalty.
